$comment: SkyTrain operating assumptions for run inference and movements (packages/transit-core/DESIGN.md#run-inference). All 'guess' unless noted; see OPEN-QUESTIONS #1–#7, #18 (answered ones are in regions/metro-vancouver/README.md). Times in seconds, distances in metres, speeds in km/h.

fleets.$comment: Lines whose trains are interchangeable, so a run may continue from one line's trip onto another's (interlining). Expo and Millennium share rolling stock and OMC 1 (diagram v3).

turnback.$minLayoverS: Minimum time from arrival at a terminus to departure of the next trip: unloading, reversing, loading (driverless trains change ends quickly). Too high and trains skip to a later departure, overfilling terminus berths. guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #6
turnback.$maxLayoverS: Longer gaps end the run (train goes to a yard) rather than waiting at the terminus.
turnback.$stubMaxLayoverS: At stub termini (Waterfront Expo/Canada, Lafarge Lake–Douglas, …) a train that would wait longer than this for a departure (in place or via the tail tracks) is surplus: it returns to the yard empty instead of occupying the platform. Operators run such trains between scheduled trains (Braden, 2026-09-26; regions/metro-vancouver/README.md#surplus-trains-at-termini; how long they wait is OPEN-QUESTIONS #21). guess
turnback.$maxPullUpM: An in-place turnback waits at the buffer of a dead-ended platform track (clear of the switch behind it) only when the buffer is within this distance of the platform stop. Farther away, the dead end is closed track, not a berth, and the train turns at the platform: Braid Platform 1, where the west track is closed beyond the platform for the OMC4 works (~430 m of it remains in OSM; Braden, 2026-09-27; regions/metro-vancouver/README.md#braid-and-the-omc4-works). Other termini pull up 9–40 m. guess
turnback.$speedFactor: Turnbacks (short empty moves between an arrival and the next departure, e.g. through the crossovers west of Production Way–University) run at this fraction of line max speed. At the pull-out speed (0.55) the 4-minute Production Way turnaround in the timetable was infeasible, so trains waited 16 min for a later departure, parked on Millennium platforms. guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #6
turnback.$reversalS: Time to change ends / reverse direction (driverless, so short). guess
turnback.$blockBonusS: Unused since GTFS block successors are now always preferred (kept for config compatibility).

yard.$comment: Pull-outs/pull-ins between yards and the first/last platform of each run (OPEN-QUESTIONS #1–#3). The nearest reachable yard by track distance is used.
yard.$pullOutLeadS: Pull-outs arrive at the first platform this long before the first departure.
yard.$deadheadSpeedFactor: Deadheads run at this fraction of line max speed: about the line's average including stops, so pull-outs don't catch up with trains in service.
yard.$runIntoYardM: How far into the yard a pulling-in train is drawn before it disappears (and a pull-out appears).
yard.$againstTrafficPenalty: Pull-outs and pull-ins keep to the normal direction of traffic: running against it costs this many extra metres per metre when choosing their path, so they take the wrong track only where it's much shorter (e.g. single-track sections). Without it, shortest paths ran empty trains against traffic over ~74 km of main line, which signalling can't allow between trains in service. guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #22
